subject: mathematics
title: Equivalent Fractions — Challenge Set 3
description: A more challenging timed set using unknowns, comparisons, and multi-step equivalence.

questions.question: Find x: 5/8 = x/40
questions.hint: Find the multiplier from 8 to 40 and apply it to 5.
questions.explanation: The denominator is multiplied by 5, so x = 5×5 = 25.

questions.question: Which statement about 6/9 and 14/21 is true?
questions.hint: Simplify both fractions before comparing them.

options.feedback: Both simplify to 2/3, so 6/9 is not greater.
Both simplify to 2/3, so 14/21 is not greater.
Both can be simplified to the same value, so they can be compared.

questions.explanation: Both fractions simplify to 2/3, so they are equal.

questions.question: Write 7/10 with denominator 50.
questions.hint: Determine how many times 10 must be multiplied to become 50.
questions.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator of 7/10 by 5 to get 35/50.

questions.question: Complete: 3/4 = 21/?
questions.hint: Use the same multiplier that changes 3 into 21.

options.feedback: 3 is multiplied by 7, so the denominator must be 4×7 = 28, not 24.
21/32 is not equivalent to 3/4; cross-products are 84 and 96.

questions.question: A learner says 8/12 and 10/15 are different values. Which conclusion is correct?
questions.hint: Reduce both fractions to simplest form.

options.text: The learner is correct because 8 and 10 are different
options.feedback: Different numerators do not mean different fraction values.

options.text: The learner is correct because 12 and 15 are different
options.feedback: Different denominators can still represent the same fraction value.

options.text: The learner is incorrect because both simplify to 2/3
The learner is incorrect because both simplify to 3/4

questions.explanation: Both fractions reduce to 2/3, so they represent the same value.
